items.title: SonicWall SMA1000 Zero-Days CVE-2026-83548 (CVSS 10.0) & CVE-2026-83549 Chained for Unauthenticated RCE — 400+ Devices Compromised
items.summary: SonicWall disclosed two critical zero-days in its SMA1000 remote-access appliances actively exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-83548 is a pre-authentication SSRF in the Work Place interface with a perfect CVSS 10.0; CVE-2026-83549 is an OS command injection in the Appliance Management Console. When chained, they enable full unauthenticated RCE without any credentials. SonicWall confirmed exploitation with over 400 internet-exposed devices already affected. Both CVEs were added to CISA's KEV catalog on September 2, 2026.
items.why: SMA1000 appliances serve as enterprise remote-access gateways — a beachhead for full network compromise. A CVSS 10.0 zero-day requiring zero authentication is as bad as it gets. Unpatched instances should be treated as fully compromised; isolate and patch immediately.

items.title: Google Emergency-Patches Actively Exploited Chrome V8 Type Confusion Zero-Day CVE-2026-85046 (CVSS 8.8) — CISA KEV Added Sept 4
items.summary: Google released an emergency Chrome stable update to fix CVE-2026-85046, a type confusion vulnerability in the V8 JavaScript/WebAssembly engine rated CVSS 8.8. The bug allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the Chrome sandbox via a crafted HTML page. Google confirmed an in-the-wild exploit exists. CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 4, 2026, mandating federal agency remediation.
items.why: Chrome is the world's most-used browser; an in-the-wild V8 exploit exposes billions of users to drive-by code execution. Enterprise IT teams should verify Chrome has auto-updated to the patched build and push the update to any managed endpoints that may lag.
items.source: The Hacker News / Google Security / CISA KEV

items.title: CISA Adds Seven Exploited Vulnerabilities to KEV on Sept 2 — Attackers Deploying Reverse Shells and Crypto Miners Across Network & AI Infrastructure
items.summary: CISA's September 2 KEV batch included seven actively exploited CVEs: CVE-2026-83548 and CVE-2026-83549 (SonicWall SMA1000), CVE-2026-82329 (JFrog Artifactory improper auth), CVE-2026-49869 (Kestra OSS command injection), CVE-2026-59822 (BerriAI LiteLLM improper auth), CVE-2026-48710 (Kludex Starlette HTTP smuggling), and CVE-2026-9586 (Sangoma Switchvox SQL injection). Threat actors are chaining these to drop reverse shells and cryptocurrency miners. 10 total CVEs hit the KEV catalog the week of Sept 1–6.
items.why: The breadth of this KEV batch is notable: AI/ML infrastructure (LiteLLM), CI/CD tooling (JFrog Artifactory), workflow automation (Kestra), and VoIP systems are all represented. Attackers are rapidly weaponizing vulnerabilities across the modern DevOps/MLOps stack — not just traditional network gear.

items.title: Palo Alto Unit42: Iranian APT 'Screening Serpens' Escalates Two-RAT-Family Espionage Campaign Across Five Countries Since Feb 2026 Conflict
items.summary: Palo Alto Unit42 published detailed tracking of Screening Serpens (Nimbus Manticore), an Iran-nexus APT assessed as one of the most active Iranian threat groups in 2026. The group dramatically escalated operations after a regional conflict began in February 2026, deploying two novel RAT families via spear-phishing — using Proton Drive-hosted lures and RAR archive attachments — against entities in five countries, consistent with strategic intelligence collection.
items.why: Two new RAT families represent a significant tooling investment, signaling a sustained, well-resourced campaign. The escalation post-February 2026 confirms Iranian state actors are using cyberspace as an active conflict instrument. Defenders in the targeted geographies — especially government, defense, and energy sectors — should hunt for the published IOCs and tighten email filtering on RAR/cloud-storage lures.

items.title: CyberStrike: Open-Source AI-Powered Autonomous Pentesting Harness with 13+ Specialized Agents, 150+ LLM Providers, and 56+ Native Offensive Tools
items.summary: CyberStrike is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) AI-native penetration testing platform updated on September 5, 2026. It wraps 150+ supported LLM providers (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Ollama for air-gapped use) with 13+ specialized offensive agents covering web apps (OWASP), mobile (Frida/Objection), cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), Active Directory, and network targets. Ships with 56+ native security tools, 7,600+ skill files, 176+ MCP integrations, and remote distributed pentesting via Bolt with Ed25519 auth.
items.why: AI-native offensive frameworks are rapidly lowering the skill floor for penetration testing — and for adversaries. CyberStrike's breadth (web, mobile, cloud, AD, network in one tool) makes it likely to see wide adoption by both red teams and threat actors. Blue teams should begin tuning detection for AI-orchestrated attack chains.
